review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the simp-tagged declarations. These were unitSMul_smul, logMap_apply, logMap_zero, logMap_one, logMap_eq_logEmbedding, intNorm_coe, quotIntNorm_apply, integerSetToAssociates_apply, integerSetQuotEquivAssociates_apply, integerSetEquiv_apply_fst, integerSetEquivNorm_apply_fst, idealSetMap_apply and mixedEmbedding_preimageOfMemIntegerSet. I found no loop or competing-rule problem among them. I grepped Mathlib for outside uses. Only Ideal/Asymptotics.lean uses mem_idealSet, and nothing outside this file uses logMap_apply, unitSMul_smul or norm_unit_smul. The two findings below are about missing simp lemmas in the idealSet/integerSet API. Both rest on in-file usage patterns, since I cannot run Lean to see how simp behaves. They are modest, not definite defects. I did not recommend simp attributes on lemmas that look simple but have no use in the file. Examples are unit_smul_eq_zero, which simp would not reach anyway because unitSMul_smul rewrites u • x first, and norm_unit_smul.

findings.excerpt:
theorem idealSetEquiv_apply (a : idealSet K J) :
    (idealSetEquiv K J a : mixedSpace K) = a := rfl
findings.problem: `idealSetEquiv` is a bundled equivalence, and these two lemmas are its coercion-to-`mixedSpace K` simp lemmas, in forward and inverse direction. Neither is tagged `@[simp]`. The analogous lemmas `idealSetMap_apply`, `integerSetEquiv_apply_fst` and `mixedEmbedding_preimageOfMemIntegerSet` are `@[simp]`. As a result `idealSetEquiv_apply` is passed by hand to `rw` in `intNorm_idealSetEquiv_apply`. `idealSetEquiv_symm_apply` is passed by hand to `rw` in `idealSetEquivNorm`. `intNorm_idealSetEquiv_apply` is fed to `simp_rw` in `card_isPrincipal_dvd_norm_le`. Any new proof about `idealSetEquiv` has to rediscover these names. The `_symm_` lemma also has an awkward proof that is only needed because it is not a `rfl`-simp lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `idealSetEquiv_apply` and `idealSetEquiv_symm_apply` as `@[simp]`. Their left sides are applications of a concrete equiv under a coercion and their right sides are strictly smaller, so I see no loop. Also consider `@[simp]` on `intNorm_idealSetEquiv_apply`, whose left side `intNorm (idealSetEquiv K J a).val` has a head symbol `intNorm` that nothing else rewrites. Since `intNorm_coe` is already simp and has the same type of right side, this keeps the normal form `mixedEmbedding.norm ↑a`.
findings.benefit: Goals that mix `intNorm`, `idealSetEquiv` and `mixedEmbedding.norm` reduce to the canonical `norm (a : mixedSpace K)` form with plain `simp`. The `simp_rw` lists in `idealSetEquivNorm` and `card_isPrincipal_dvd_norm_le` get shorter. It also gives later Mathlib users of `idealSet` (for example `Ideal/Asymptotics.lean`) the same simp interface that `integerSet` already has.

evidence.excerpt: theorem idealSetMap_apply (a : idealSet K J) : (idealSetMap K J a : mixedSpace K) = a := rfl

findings.problem: This is the left-inverse companion of the `@[simp]` lemma `mixedEmbedding_preimageOfMemIntegerSet`. It is the canonical simplification of `preimageOfMemIntegerSet ⟨mixedEmbedding K x, hx⟩` to `x`. It is not tagged `@[simp]`, although the file itself applies it inside `simp_rw`, in `preimage_of_IdealSetMap`. Only one direction of the round trip is therefore available to `simp`. The statement also carries redundant `(x : 𝓞 K)` ascriptions and parentheses.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `preimageOfMemIntegerSet_mixedEmbedding`, and drop the redundant `(x : 𝓞 K)` ascriptions. The left side is headed by `preimageOfMemIntegerSet` applied to an explicit `Subtype.mk`, which only matches when the subtype value has the form `mixedEmbedding K x`. The right side is the variable `x`, and `hx` is a proof argument, so I expect no loop. It does not overlap with `mixedEmbedding_preimageOfMemIntegerSet`, which has a different head symbol.
findings.benefit: Round trips through `preimageOfMemIntegerSet` close with plain `simp`. At the moment each such call site must name this lemma, as `preimage_of_IdealSetMap` does.
